Rashi on Shabbat 69b:1:1.hebrew: קמ"ל - אביי, דמודה רבי יוחנן בה דבעינן שגגת לאו — דאי הזיד בלאו, תו ליכא שגגה; דבהא נמי פליגי רבנן אמונבז, ואמרי דאין שגגת קרבן שגגה:
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:1:1.english: Teaches us - Abaye [teaches us] that Rabbi Yoḥanan concedes in this [case] that we require unwittingness regarding the negative prohibition; for if he acted intentionally regarding the negative prohibition, there is no longer any unwittingness, as in this [case] as well, the Rabbis disagree with Munbaz and say that unwittingness regarding an offering is not [considered] unwittingness.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:1:2.hebrew: איזהו שבועת ביטוי לשעבר - בשלמא להבא, כגון "שלא אוכל", משכחת לה, כגון שנתעלמה השבועה ואכל; אלא לשעבר, כגון "שאכלתי" והוא לא אכל — אין כאן שוגג, דאי כסבור שאכל בשעה שנשבע, אינו חייב קרבן, דתניא בשבועות (פ"ג דף כו.): "האדם בשבועה" — פרט לאנוס; כלומר, "האדם בשבועה" — שיהא אדם בשעת שבועה, שתהא דעתו עליו בשעת שבועה, ופרשינן לה התם לאפוקי כי האי גוונא. ומהשתא, לא משכחת שגגה אלא בקרבן:
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:1:2.english: What is an oath on a statement relating to the past - It is understandable regarding [an oath relating to] the future, such as [if one swore,] "that I will not eat," [how] you find [an unwitting violation] — such as where the oath slipped his mind and he ate. But regarding [an oath relating to] the past, such as [if one swore,] "that I ate," and he had not eaten, there is no unwitting [violation] here; for if he believed that he had eaten at the time he swore, he is not liable to bring an offering, as it was taught in a baraita in Shevuot (chapter 3, daf 26a): "[...which] a person [may utter] with an oath" — excluding one who acts under circumstances beyond his control; that is to say, "a person with an oath" — that he must be a person [of sound mind] at the time of the oath, that his mind must be with him at the time of the oath, and we explained there that this excludes this type of case. And from now on, you cannot find an unwitting violation except regarding the offering.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:1:3.english: He said: "I know that I am swearing falsely" - And I was warned about this.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:1:4.hebrew: אבל איני יודע כו' - דאי בנתעלמה ממנו אזהרת שבועה, אין לך אונס בשעת שבועה כזה:
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:1:4.english: But I do not know, etc. - For if the warning against [taking an] oath was concealed from him, there is no greater circumstance beyond one's control at the time of an oath than this.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:1:5.english: [He is] liable - Evidently the Rabbis agree in this case that one is liable for ignorance regarding the sacrifice.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:1:6.hebrew: הא מני מונבז היא - דאמר נמי בעלמא שמה שגגה, אבל לרבנן דפליגי עליה לית להו ביטוי לשעבר, דסברי כר' ישמעאל דאמר בשבועות אינו חייב אלא על העתיד לבא (שם דף כה.). יש גורסין: הא מני? מונבז — פשיטא! השתא בכל התורה אמר מונבז שגגת קרבן שמה שגגה, הכא דחידוש הוא לא כ"ש?! אלא לאו רבנן, תיובתא דאביי — תיובתא. ולא נהירא לי: דמאי פשיטותא? הא איצטריך לאשמעינן דחלוקה שגגה זו משאר שגגות, דאילו בכל התורה למונבז, בין ששגג בקרבן בין ששגג בלאו וכרת — שמה שגגה; וכאן בלשעבר, אם שגג בלאו שבה — לאו שגגה היא, דכתיב: האדם בשבועה:
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:1:6.english: In accordance with whose opinion is this? It is Munbaz - For he also says in general that [unawareness of an offering] is considered unwitting [transgression]. But according to the Rabbis who disagree with him, they do not accept [liability for an offering for an oath on] a statement [relating to the] past, as they hold in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael, who says in [tractate] Shevuot that one is liable only for [an oath regarding] the future (there, 25a). Some have the reading: 'In accordance with whose opinion is this? [If you say it is] Munbaz — it is obvious! Now, if throughout the whole Torah Munbaz said that unwittingness regarding an offering is considered unwittingness, here, where [the obligation of an offering] is a novelty, is it not all the more so?! Rather, is it not [the opinion of] the Rabbis, and [thus it is a] refutation of Abaye? [Indeed, it is] a refutation!' And [this reading] does not seem correct to me, for why is it obvious? Behold, it was necessary to teach us that this [case of] unwittingness is different from other [cases of] unwittingness: for throughout the whole Torah, according to Munbaz, whether one was unwitting regarding the offering or unwitting regarding the negative prohibition and excision, it is considered unwitting; whereas here, regarding [an oath on the] past, if one was unwitting regarding the negative prohibition in it, it is not [considered] an unwitting [transgression], as it is written: 'A person [who utters] with an oath' [Leviticus 5:4].

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:3:1.hebrew: הכל מודים בתרומה - זר שאכל תרומה בשוגג משלם חומש על שגגתו, דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ב:י״ד): "ואיש כי יאכל קדש בשגגה". אבל מזיד — אין מוסיף חומש, וחייב מיתה בידי שמים, דכתיב (שם): "ומתו בו כי יחללוהו", וסמיך ליה: "וכל זר לא יאכל קדש":
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:3:1.english: Everyone agrees with regard to teruma - A non-priest who ate teruma unwittingly pays a fifth for his unwitting act, as it is written: “And if a man eats of the holy thing unwittingly” (Leviticus 22:14). But an intentional offender does not add a fifth, and is liable to death at the hand of Heaven, as it is written: “and die therein, if they profane it” (ibid. 9), and juxtaposed to it: “There shall no non-priest eat of the holy thing” (ibid. 10).

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:3:2.hebrew: בלאו שבה - כסבור חולין, ואין כאן לאו:
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:3:2.english: With regard to the negative prohibition in it - Thinking [it was] non-sacred [food], and [thus that] there is no negative prohibition here.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:3:3.english: Death - Which is written with regard to teruma.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:3:4.english: In place of karet - Of other transgressions.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:3:5.hebrew: וחומש - דשגגת תרומה במקום קרבן דשגגת שאר עבירות. ולרבי יוחנן, מיחייב חומש אשגגת מיתה:
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:3:5.english: And the fifth - [The fifth] of an unwitting [act involving] teruma [stands] in place of a sacrifice for an unwitting [act involving] other transgressions. And according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, one is liable [to pay] a fifth for [being] unwitting with regard to death.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:4:1.hebrew: מונה ו' - מיום ששם אל לבו שכחתו, ומשמר השביעי:
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:4:1.english: Counts six - From the day that he took note of his forgetfulness, and observes the seventh [day].

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:4:2.hebrew: משמר יום אחד ומונה ו' - וכל יום ששם אל לבו אינו משמר, דשמא עשה מלאכה, אבל יום המחרת משמר. ולקמן מפרש, דבהנך דאינו משמר לא עביד נמי מלאכה, אלא כדי פרנסת היום:
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:4:2.english: He observes one day and counts six - And that whole day on which he took [it] to heart he does not observe [it], for perhaps he [already] performed work; but the following day he observes [it]. And later, [the Gemara] explains that on those [days] that he does not observe, he also does not perform work, except for [what is needed for] that day's sustenance.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:4:3.english: Like the creation of the world - The weekdays were counted first.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:4:4.hebrew: כאדם הראשון - שנברא בע"ש, ויום ראשון למנינו שבת היה:
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:4:4.english: Like Adam the first [man] - Who was created on the eve of Shabbat, and the first day of his count was Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:4:5.hebrew: יום אחד לששה - משמע לו' שעברו:
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:4:5.english: One day for six - [This] implies for the six [days] that have passed.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:6:1.english: And on that day let him die? - [This is asked] in astonishment.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:6:2.english: And perhaps yesterday was Shabbat - And he would turn out to be desecrating Shabbat not for the sake of saving a life.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:6:3.hebrew: בקדושתא ואבדלתא - לזכרון בעלמא, שיהא לו שם יום חלוק משאר ימים, ולא תשתכח שבת ממנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:6:3.english: Through kiddush and havdala - Merely for remembrance, so that he will have the designation of a day distinct from the other days, and Shabbat will not be forgotten by him.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:7:1.hebrew: אם היה מכיר מקצת יום שיצא בו - לא שזכר איזה יום בשבת היה, אלא זכור שהיום יום שלישי ליציאתו או רביעי ליציאתו, ומתוך כך ידע שמונה ליציאתו — עושה מלאכה כל יום ח', וכן לעולם. ודאי זהו יום שיצא בו, וקים ליה דבשבת לא יצא, שהרי בישוב לא שכח את השבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:7:1.english: If he had partial knowledge of the day on which he left - Not that he remembered which day of the week it was, but rather he remembers that today is the third day since his departure, or the fourth day since his departure, and through this he knows [when it is] eight [days] since his departure — he may perform labor on every eighth day, and so on forever. It is certain that this is the day on which he left, and he is certain that he did not leave on Shabbat, for while in a settled area he had not forgotten the Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:7:2.hebrew: במעלי שבתא נמי לא נפיק - דאין דרך לצאת מפני כבוד השבת. ועל כן, כל יום ח' וט' ליציאתו לישתרו, דליכא לספוקינהו בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:7:2.english: He also did not leave on the eve of Shabbat - For it is not customary to set out [on a journey], out of respect for Shabbat. And therefore, every eighth and ninth day [counting] from his departure should be permitted [for labor], as they cannot be suspected of being Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:8:1.hebrew: מנא הני מילי - שיש מחלל בשבתות הרבה וחייב אחת על כולן, ויש מחללן וחייב על כל שבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:8:1.english: From where are these matters [derived] - That there is [one who] desecrates [the Sabbath] across many Sabbaths and is liable [for only] one [sin-offering] for all of them, and there is [one who] desecrates them and is liable for each Sabbath.

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:8:2.hebrew: הכי גרסינן הא כיצד ושמרו בני ישראל את השבת שמירה אחת לשבתות הרבה ואת שבתותי תשמורו שמירה לכל שבת ושבת - דקרא קמא חדא שבת הוא דחשיב, משמע שאינו מקפיד אלא על האחת. והכא כתיב "את שבתותי" — אכולהו קפיד. ולא מסרן אלא לחכמים, להודיען מסברא: האי — בשכח עיקר שבת, דחדא שגגה היא; והאי — בשוכח שהיום שבת, אבל יודע עיקר שבת, דאיכא למימר: ימים שבינתים [הויין] ידיעה לחלק:
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:8:2.english: This is our reading: "How so? 'And the children of Israel shall observe the Shabbat' — one observance for many Shabbatot; 'and you shall observe My Shabbatot' — [one] observance for each and every Shabbat" - For the first verse mentions [only] one Shabbat, which implies that He is exacting only regarding one. And here it is written "My Shabbatot" — He is exacting regarding all of them. And He handed them over only to the Sages to determine them through logical reasoning: this [first verse applies] to one who forgot the essence of Shabbat, as it is a single unwitting lapse; and this [second verse applies] to one who forgets that today is Shabbat, but knows the essence of Shabbat, for it can be said [that] the intervening days [constitute] awareness to divide [the transgressions into separate liabilities].

Rashi on Shabbat 69b:9:1.hebrew: איפכא מסתברא - ״ושמרו בני ישראל את השבת״ משמע שמירה אחת לשבת אחת, ו״את שבתותי תשמורו״ — ב' שבתות, ואינו מזהיר אלא על שמירה אחת. ובין רב נחמן ובין רב נחמן בר יצחק לא פליגי אלא במשמעותא: מאי דיליף מר מהאי קרא, יליף מר מאידך:
Rashi on Shabbat 69b:9:1.english: The opposite is reasonable - “And the children of Israel shall observe the Shabbat” implies one observance for one Shabbat; and “And you shall observe My Shabbatot” [mentions] two Shabbatot, yet it cautions regarding only one observance. And between Rav Naḥman and Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak, they disagree only regarding the interpretation: what one Master derives from this verse, the [other] Master derives from the other.

Tosafot on Shabbat 69b:1:1.hebrew: הא מני מונבז היא - פירש בקונטרס: אבל לרבנן דפליגי אמונבז, לא אשכחן שגגת שבועת ביטוי לשעבר; וסברי כרבי ישמעאל, דאמר בשבועות דאינו חייב אלא על העתיד לבא. והקשה ה"ר אליעזר לרבינו שמואל: דהא רבנן דמונבז — רבי עקיבא, ור"ע מחייב בהדיא על לשעבר בשבועות [פ"ג; וכלשון אחר שפי' בקונטרס, מוכח בשבועות] בפ"ג (דף כו:), דאמר: בעא מיניה רבא מרב נחמן: איזהו שגגת ביטוי לשעבר? אמר ליה: כגון דאמר יודע אני ששבועה זו אסורה, אבל איני יודע אם חייבין עליה קרבן אם לאו; ופריך ליה: כמאן, כמונבז? ומשני: אפילו תימא רבנן, אע"ג דבכל התורה כולה לית להו שגגה בקרבן, כו'. ומה שהקשה בקונטרס: מאי פשיטא? הא קמ"ל: אף על גב דבעלמא הוי שגגה, הכא לאו שגגה היא, משום ד"האדם בשבועה" בעינן — לאו פירכא היא; דאי משום הא איצטריך, ליתני בהדיא: "האדם בשבועה" — פרט לאנוס, אלא משמע דשגגת קרבן אתא לאשמעינן ששמה שגגה. ומיהו קשה, דבלאו הך ברייתא הוה מצי למיפרך לאביי ממתניתין דשבועות, דמחייב ר"ע שבועת ביטוי לשעבר, ולא משכחת לה אלא אם כן הזיד בלאו! על כן נראה כפירוש רבינו שמואל שהשיב: לרבנן, דשגגת קרבן לאו שמה שגגה, משכחת שגגת שבועת ביטוי לשעבר, כגון שיודע ששבועה זו אסורה אבל אינו יודע שיש בה לאו, אבל סבור שיש בה איסור עשה, וחשיב שפיר "האדם בשבועה" בענין זה. וכן מוכח בשבועות (שם), דמ"האדם בשבועה" לא ממעט אלא כסבור בשעת שבועה שבאמת נשבע, כגון תלמידי דרב, דמר משתבע דהכי אמר רב כו'. הלכך: "הא מני מונבז הוא" — דלרבנן הוה ליה למיתני: "ואינו יודע אם חייבין עליה לאו". וההוא דשבועות דבעא מיניה רבא מרב נחמן — פליגא אדאביי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 69b:1:1.english: In accordance with whose opinion is this? It is Munbaz: Rashi explained: But according to the Rabbis who dispute Munbaz, we do not find [any case of] an unwitting past statement-oath; and they hold in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael, who said in Shevuot that one is liable only for [an oath relating to] the future. And R. Eliezer raised a difficulty to Rabbeinu Shmuel: Behold, the Rabbis [who dispute] Munbaz are Rabbi Akiva, and Rabbi Akiva explicitly holds one liable for [an oath relating to] the past in Shevuot [chapter 3; and according to the other version that [Rashi] explained in the commentary, it is proven in Shevuot] in chapter 3 (26b), where it says: Rava inquired of Rav Nachman: "What is an unwitting past statement-oath?" He said to him: "For example, where he says: 'I know that this oath is prohibited, but I do not know whether or not one is liable to bring an offering for it.'" And [Rava] raised an objection to him: "In accordance with whose opinion? Munbaz?" And [Rav Nachman] answered: "You may even say [it is in accordance with] the Rabbis; even though in the entire Torah they do not hold that ignorance of an offering [is considered an unwitting transgression], etc." And that which [Rashi] questioned in the commentary: "Why would it be obvious? This comes to teach us: even though elsewhere it is considered an unwitting transgression, here it is not considered an unwitting transgression because we require [the fulfillment of the verse] 'expressed by a person' (Leviticus 5:4)" — this is not a valid refutation; for if it was needed because of that, it should have taught explicitly: "'Expressed by a person' — excluding one under duress"! Rather, it implies that it comes to teach us that ignorance of an offering is considered an unwitting transgression. However, it is difficult: for even without this baraita, [the Gemara] could have raised an objection against Abaye from the Mishnah in Shevuot, where Rabbi Akiva holds one liable for a past statement-oath, and you cannot find [a case where one is liable] unless he was intentional regarding the negative commandment! Therefore, it appears in accordance with the explanation of Rabbeinu Shmuel, who replied: According to the Rabbis, that ignorance of an offering is not considered an unwitting transgression, you can find [a case of] an unwitting past statement-oath, such as where he knows that this oath is prohibited, but he does not know that it contains a negative commandment, but rather thinks that it contains a positive commandment; and in this manner, it is properly considered "expressed by a person." And so it is proven in Shevuot (ibid.), that from "expressed by a person," [the verse] excludes only one who at the time of the oath believed that he was swearing truthfully, such as the students of Rav, where one master swears that this is what Rav said, etc. Therefore, "In accordance with whose opinion is this? It is Munbaz" — for according to the Rabbis, it should have taught: "and he does not know whether one is liable to a negative commandment for it." And that [passage] in Shevuot where Rava inquired of Rav Nachman disagrees with Abaye.

Tosafot on Shabbat 69b:6:1.hebrew: עושה כדי פרנסתו - אבל להלך יכול כל מה שירצה, רק ביום שמשמר; דאי לאו הכי, לא יגיע לעולם ליישוב. והא דקאמר "במאי מינכר" — משום דאין זה היכר שבת במה שיושב ואינו הולך. אי נמי: אפי' ביום שמשמר הולך כמו שרוצה, והשתא לא מינכר אלא בקידושא. הרב פור"ת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 69b:6:1.english: He makes enough for his sustenance - However, as for walking, he may [walk] as much as he wants, except on the day that he observes; for if not so, he would never reach an inhabited area. And as for that which [the Gemara] says, "By what is it distinguishable?" — [this is asked] because there is no [sufficient] recognition of Shabbat in his sitting and not walking. Alternatively: even on the day that he observes, he walks as much as he wants, and now it is distinguishable only through kiddush. Rabbeinu Porat.
